newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power moves higher on outage talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power moves higher on outage talk.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West generally moved higher Monday on talk of possible supply constraints from coal and nuclear power plant outages, industry sources said.
"There are a few units out so prices did move higher," one northeast power marketer said.

In Michigan, American Electric Power's 1,020 megawatt (MW) Cook 1 nuclear plant was shut over the weekend for repairs but was expected to return to service Monday and gradually build output back to 100 percent.
Also Commonwealth Edison Co's 1,078 MW LaSalle 1 unit in Illinois was expected to resume electricity production on Wednesday after being shut down over the weekend for repairs.

The Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) bucked the push higher however, with some line loading keeping power prices down in the region due to limited export capability, the brokers and marketers said.
MAPP on peak electricity for a 16-hour block for delivery Tuesday was talked in the $12.00-13.00 range from Monday delivery discussion near $13.00-15.00 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak power was pegged in the $7.50-9.00 range from weekend talk in the $7.50-8.00 range.

On-peak prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Tuesday delivery were said to be discussed in the $16.50-19.00 per MWh range next day from talk at $14.00-15.00 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak power was said to be in the $9.50-11.00 range from talk at $8.00-9.00 last week, the sources said.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Tuesday delivery were quoted at 14.25-16.25 from $14.00-16.00 last week.
Off peak ECAR was said to be bid near $11.50 for next-day delivery.
ECAR peak power prices for the remainder of September were said to be bid at $18.25, while power for all of October was discussed in the $16.75-17.50 range, the sources said.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Tuesday delivery in the north area was assessed in the $13.00-15.50 range from discussion at $13.00-14.00 late last week, while in the south, power was pegged at $16.50-18.50 from discussion at 16.00-16.50 last week, the sources said.
Off-peak SPP in the north was said to be near $11.00-12.00.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
